correctness.rationale: For all integers N>=2 the explicit two vectors have disjoint support and squared norms 1, and the explicit symmetric parent has eigenvalues 1, 2 and 3. Arnoldi from u gives v exactly. All full-rank two-row selections lie in four exhaustive classes; beta>gamma>epsilon gives exactly the N E-optimal row pairs at condition sqrt(N), while {2,3} alone has condition 1. Both DEIM and pivoted-QR Q-DEIM choose row1 and then a j>=4. Orthogonality of V and the QR factor imply kappa(V R^-1)=kappa(SV). The finite checker tested 95,274 cases plus numerical pivots but the algebraic proof establishes the all-N claim.

value.rationale: The 2026 Krylov sketch method explicitly uses maximum minimum singular value to control a whitening condition metric, so a sharp unlimited gap between the criteria is a motivated methodological boundary rather than an arbitrary invariant. The result persists with SPD A condition number 3, is attained by both named pivot algorithms, and covers every ideal criterion maximizer. It prevents interpreting E-optimality as a constant-factor guarantee for the actual metric, without claiming the tiny-amplitude alternative is numerically superior.
